title: Policy engine: guardrails for rollout actions (step size, soak time, approvals)
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: Hosted canary rollouts GA requires enforceable guardrails on *actions* (create/start/progress/pause/resume/rollback) so customers can’t accidentally (or maliciously) exceed approved step sizes, skip minimum soak times, or bypass required approvals. This PR adds rollout-specific policy checks to the policy engine and wires them into the Console backend error contract (human-readable messages + stable error codes). Scope: (1) step size guardrails: max traffic jump per step (e.g., 1%→25% disallowed if max_step_increase_pct=10) with special-case handling for rollback; (2) soak time guardrails: minimum soak duration between step changes, with explicit override only when the actor has a higher-privilege permission; (3) approval gates: per-action approvals (e.g., requiring rollout_approver for start and/or step changes past N%) with consistent denial semantics; (4) error mapping: policy denials return structured errors that Console can render as inline validation + blocking modal errors; (5) auditability hooks: include policy decision context in the denial payload so orchestrator/Console can log why an action was denied (note: audit event emission itself is in a separate PR). Implementation notes: - Added new resource type `rollout_action` to policy engine with `action_type`, `route_id`, `rollout_id`, `from_canary_pct`, `to_canary_pct`, `time_since_last_step_seconds`, and `requires_approval` as inputs. - Guardrails are computed from effective policy (tenant defaults + route overrides) resolved via existing config layering. - Approval checks integrate with RBAC: `rollouts.approve` permission gates actions when approval_required=true, and also gates override paths (e.g., early step progression before min soak). - Deny reasons are normalized into `POLICY_DENIED` with subcodes: `ROLLOUT_MAX_STEP_EXCEEDED`, `ROLLOUT_MIN_SOAK_NOT_MET`, `ROLLOUT_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `ROLLOUT_OVERRIDE_NOT_PERMITTED`, `ROLLOUT_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE`. - Added test matrix covering: small jumps, large jumps, rollback to 0, step changes at/over boundary, soak timers, and approver vs non-approver actors. - Console backend integration: updated policy client to pass full rollout action context; maps denial subcodes to the existing Console contract (rendered as “You can’t increase traffic by more than 10% per step” etc.). Out of scope: quality gates, dynamic traffic optimization, and Dedicated/Private behavior (schema remains compatible, but enforcement here is Hosted action policy only). Risk/rollout: policy evaluation is behind `hosted_rollouts_policy_guardrails` flag; when disabled, engine falls back to existing coarse allow/deny behavior. Follow-ups: align defaults with SRE recommended beta thresholds (tracked in ENG-9158/ENG-9152) and wire denial payload into audit events (ENG-9171).

policy: enforce max step increase guardrail + rollback exception
policy: enforce min soak time + override permission
policy: approval gating for start/progress actions
console-backend: map policy denial subcodes to user-facing errors

docs(internal): update policy engine README for rollout_action
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can you clarify precedence when both tenant default and route override specify max_step_increase_pct? Also, how are we handling action attempts while rollout is paused?

Jordan Lee (author): Precedence matches existing config layering: route override wins over tenant default; if unset on route, tenant default applies. For paused rollouts, `ROLLOUT_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_STATE` denies progress, but allows rollback and resume (resume requires approval if configured). Added explicit state matrix tests in guardrails.test.ts.

Chloe Martin: Console needs stable subcodes. Please avoid embedding numbers in the code (e.g., MAX_STEP_10). Also make sure the denial message is actionable for end users and includes next allowed step.

Jordan Lee (author): Updated to fixed subcodes only (no numeric variants). Message template now includes computed next_allowed_canary_pct and min_soak_remaining_seconds so Console can show “Next allowed: 15%” and “Try again in ~8m” where relevant.
Marcus Lin: For overrides (skip soak / exceed step), are we checking a distinct permission vs rollouts.approve? I’d prefer least privilege: approval != override.

Jordan Lee (author): Agreed. Split permissions: approvals use `rollouts.approve`; overrides require `rollouts.override_guardrails`. Wired both through RBAC and added tests. Default bundles do not grant override to rollout-approver.
Benji Okafor: Concern about policy evaluation cost. We’re adding new inputs and more logic. Any perf impact measured?

Jordan Lee (author): Added a micro-benchmark in policy-engine (eval 10k actions). Δ ~2.1% p95 eval time due to extra branching, within budget. Also cached effective guardrail config per route_id for the request lifetime to avoid repeated YAML resolution.
Chloe Martin: One more: Console currently surfaces only one error. If multiple guardrails fail, which one do we show?

Jordan Lee (author): Deterministic ordering: state validity -> approval required -> max step -> min soak. Rationale: approvals/state are the primary blockers; step/soak are secondary. Documented in `guardrails.ts` header and added a test to lock ordering.
Ethan Park: Looks good. Please add a short note in defaults file about recommended values for beta vs GA (even if we keep GA defaults conservative).
Jordan Lee (author): Added comments in `config/policy/defaults/hosted_rollouts.yaml` referencing PM-1851 and that SRE tuning is tracked in ENG-9158.
release_notes: Added policy engine guardrails for Hosted rollout actions: max step increase, minimum soak time, and approval gates.
Console backend now displays actionable validation messages when a rollout action is denied by policy.
Introduced distinct permission for guardrail overrides (separate from rollout approvals).
